title: I AM (Exodus 3:13–15)
hookLine: asked his name, God answers I AM THAT I AM

cards: At the bush, God gives Moses a job: go back to Egypt and bring my people out. Moses has questions. The first is: who am I, to go to Pharaoh?
The second is sharper. Suppose the Israelites ask, what is his name? What do I tell them?
Jacob asked it too, after wrestling all night by the river: "Tell me, I pray thee, thy name." He got a blessing instead of an answer. Moses wants something to say.
What he gets is not a name like any other.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you." In Hebrew it's three words: ehyeh asher ehyeh.
Ehyeh comes from the verb to be.

teach.h: I AM, OR I WILL BE.
teach.b: It can mean I am who I am, or I will be what I will be. Scholars still argue, and the honest answer is that the Hebrew holds both. A name that won't sit still: not a statue you can carry, not a label you can control.

teach.h: FOUR LETTERS: Y, H, W, H.
teach.b: Then God adds the name Israel will use, four Hebrew letters, Y, H, W, H, closely related to that verb to be. "This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations."
Out of reverence, Jews stopped saying it aloud long ago.
When they read it, they say Adonai, my Lord, or call it simply HaShem, the Name. The King James Bible follows a similar path: wherever you see LORD in small capital letters, that's this name.
The English word Jehovah came later, from combining the four letters with the vowels of Adonai. How it was first pronounced, nobody knows for certain.
Christians hear this name again in the Gospel of John, where Jesus says, "Before Abraham was, I am."
Christian tradition hears in it the name from the bush. So God doesn't give Moses a title. God gives him a verb: I am.

how: The King James Bible, like many English Bibles, prints the divine name as LORD in small capitals, following the Jewish practice of not pronouncing it, and Christians read the "I am" sayings in John's Gospel alongside Exodus 3:14.

games.q: you're Moses. you've asked God for a name to give the Israelites, something solid, something you can say to them. what do you hear?
o: a title: the God of Egypt's enemies.
a verb: I AM THAT I AM.
games.why: "I AM THAT I AM... say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you." a name that is a verb, and won't sit still.

practice: On the in-breath, let the word am rise in your mind; on the out-breath, let it go. No words after it, not tired, not late, not failing, just am.
If you pray, let it point toward the one who said I am; if you don't, simply rest in being here.

wordCard.voice: YHWH. The four-letter name of God given at the bush, linked to the verb to be, and printed LORD in the King James Bible.

orig.say: not spoken aloud in Jewish practice; read as ah-doh-NAI
orig.note: Hebrew: the four-letter name of God, linked to the verb to be. its original pronunciation is uncertain.
